title: Action-site cohomology of a filtered colimit of equivariant condensed modules
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small site $P$ of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, and let $\mathcal A_J(R)$ be internal $R$-modules with $R$-linear actions of $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$, natural in profinite parameters [def-sfb-condensed-action-module, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category (nonempty, and every finite diagram has a cocone) and $N:I\to\mathcal A_J(R)$ a diagram with a colimit cocone $(\iota_i:N_i\to L)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathcal A_J(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Use the site $P_J$ of profinite continuous left $J$-spaces with finite jointly surjective equivariant coverings, the coefficient ring sheaf $\mathcal R_J=\Phi(R)$, and the exact additive equivalence $\Phi:\mathcal A_J(R)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R_J)$ normalized by $\Phi(M)(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(P)^{\underline J}}(h_T,M)$, as specified in [lem-sfb-profinite-action-coherent-presentation]. Here $h_T(S)=C(S,T)$, $R$ has trivial action, and $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R_J)$ means sheaves of modules over this ring sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

Put $F_i=\Phi(N_i)$ and $F=\Phi(L)$. The maps $\Phi(\iota_i)$ exhibit $F$ as their colimit in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R_J)$, and their underlying abelian maps exhibit $F_{ab}$ as $\operatorname{colim}_i(F_i)_{ab}$. For every object $T\in P_J$ and $q\geq0$, object cohomology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives an isomorphism
$$c_{T,q}:\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(T,(F_i)_{ab})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T,F_{ab}),$$
whose $i$-leg is exactly $H^q(T,\Phi(\iota_i)_{ab})$. The maps $c_{T,q}$ commute with every restriction along an equivariant map $T'\to T$ and with morphisms of diagrams $N\to N'$ and the induced map of the chosen colimits. In particular they give an isomorphism of abelian presheaves on $P$ after $T=tS$, where $tS$ is $S$ with trivial action. All sites, parameters, cohomology groups and indexing categories are in the compatible universes fixed above.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-profinite-action-coherent-presentation], $P_J$ is small, has finite limits, and has finite covering families stable under pullback and finite composition. An equivariant isomorphism is surjective on underlying spaces, so its singleton family is a finite jointly surjective covering. Thus every finite-cover-site hypothesis used below is satisfied. The same node supplies the specified equivalence $\Phi$. Apply [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] to this equivalence and the given colimit cocone of $N$: the cocone with vertex $F=\Phi(L)$ and legs $\lambda_i=\Phi(\iota_i):F_i\to F$ is colimiting in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R_J)$. Preservation is of this cocone, so its legs are the original transported maps.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact; applied to the normalized equivalence in the coherent-presentation node.

proof.text: Check the sheafification hypothesis for the general module-sheaf colimit theorem. Abelian groups are $\mathbb Z$-modules: the action is $n\cdot x=x+\cdots+x$ for $n\ge0$, and its negative for $n<0$; every additive map preserves it. Thus the Grothendieck-abelian assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian] at $R=\mathbb Z$ applies to $\operatorname{Ab}$ in the chosen coefficient universe. Since $P_J$ is small in that universe, [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification] gives sheafification of every abelian presheaf on $P_J$. Here the universe is the compatible one fixed in the statement, rather than an enlargement of the indexing category.

source.place: Tag 079B, definition-grothendieck-conditions, and Algebra Tag 00DB; general small-site coefficient sheafification as stated in lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification.

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] on $P_J$ with the ring sheaf $\mathcal R_J$; its sheafification assumption was checked in step 2. The forgetful functor sends the colimiting cocone of step 1 to a colimiting cocone in abelian sheaves. Consequently $F_{ab}$, with legs $(\lambda_i)_{ab}$, is a colimit of the diagram $(F_i)_{ab}$. This uses the theorem for an arbitrary ring sheaf, not a constant-coefficient or an etale-site specialization.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, forgetful functor to abelian sheaves commutes with colimits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-cover-derived-presheaf-continuity] to the finite-cover site $P_J$, the small filtered category $I$, and the abelian colimit cocone of step 3. The hypotheses are precisely those checked in step 1; the diagram retains all its morphisms, including parallel arrows. The cited statement gives an isomorphism $\delta$ in the derived category of abelian presheaves and explicitly identifies the evaluation of $H^q(\delta)$ at $T$ with the actual coprojection-induced map $c_{T,q}:\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(T,(F_i)_{ab})\to H^q(T,F_{ab})$. Since a functor sends an inverse to an inverse, $H^q(\delta)$ and its evaluation are isomorphisms. Under the cited identifications, for each source coprojection $j_{i,T}$ the map therefore satisfies $c_{T,q}j_{i,T}=H^q(T,(\lambda_i)_{ab})=H^q(T,(\Phi(\iota_i))_{ab})$. This proves both the comparison isomorphism and its specified legs using the current node statement; no construction from its proof or change of index category is used.

source.place: Tag 09YP, lemma-colimit, constant-site specialization with initial zero coefficient; derived-presheaf and original-leg formulation in lem-sfb-finite-cover-derived-presheaf-continuity.

proof.text: The continuity identification is natural in $T$ and in coefficient diagrams by [lem-sfb-finite-cover-derived-presheaf-continuity]. Explicitly, if $r:T\to T\!\prime$ is an equivariant map, both composites in its restriction square send a stage class $j_{i,T\!\prime}(x)$ to $H^q(T,(\lambda_i)_{ab})(r^*x)$. For a diagram morphism $a:N\to N\!\prime$ and its induced colimit map $b:L\to L\!\prime$, the equation $b\iota_i=\iota_i\!\prime a_i$ gives, after $\Phi$, forgetting scalars and $H^q(T,-)$, equality of the two comparison composites on every stage. Maps out of a colimit are determined by these legs, which proves both squares commute for the chosen colimits. Finally, the trivial-action functor $t:P\to P_J$ and its behavior on parameter maps are supplied by [lem-sfb-profinite-action-coherent-presentation]. Restrict the natural family $c_{T,q}$ along $t$. Its components are isomorphisms, so their inverses commute with the restriction maps as well (multiply the naturality equation by the two inverses). This is the claimed isomorphism of abelian presheaves on $P$.
